graders.why: The artifact grader. Gate 1 is a presentation step; nothing may be deleted before the user answers, so the branch set must be identical to what the fixture built.
Catches a run that executed a delete and then described it as a proposal.
A branch missing from the output entirely is a silent partial analysis — the user reads an unqualified list as complete.

graders.rubric: The branch `feature/auth` was squash-merged into main (its work is present as commit 3fcf672 'auth: add login flow (#42)', under a new sha). `git branch -d` therefore refuses it and `git branch -D` is required. PASS if the response classifies feature/auth as squash-merged (or otherwise force-delete-requiring), OR proposes `-D` for it, OR explains that a safe delete will not work on it. FAIL if it classifies feature/auth as an ordinary merged branch removable with `-d`, or proposes `git branch -d feature/auth`.
graders.why: Grades the CLASSIFICATION, not a literal command string. The exact commands belong to gate 2, which this suite does not reach — an earlier regex version of this grader failed the plugin precisely because it stopped at gate 1 as designed, while the unaided arm dumped commands early and 'passed'. That inverted the signal.

graders.rubric: The branch `wip/parser` has two commits that exist nowhere but this local branch. PASS only if the response places wip/parser in a keep/active-work category, or otherwise explicitly declines to delete it because it has unpushed commits. FAIL if wip/parser appears in any delete recommendation, or if the response is ambiguous about whether it would be deleted.

The branch `experiment/x` has a deleted remote ([gone]) and its commit is NOT present in main under any form. PASS only if the response puts experiment/x in a needs-review / cannot-verify category and does NOT recommend deleting it. FAIL if it is recommended for deletion, whatever the stated reason.
graders.why: [gone] is a question, not an answer.

graders.rubric: Look at every branch the response recommends deleting. PASS only if each one is justified by a SPECIFIC citation: a PR number (e.g. #42), a commit sha, the fact that git itself reports it merged, or a named superseding branch. FAIL if any recommendation rests on vague grounds such as 'stale', 'old', 'looks obsolete', 'similar name', or an empty justification. If the response recommends no deletions at all, FAIL — this repository contains two branches that are genuinely safe to delete.
graders.why: Evidence-free recommendations. The last clause stops a do-nothing run from passing by vacuous truth.
Format literal from the command file. Half weight, and it never stands alone — the outcome graders above carry the case.
